title: Godot or Unity for 3D game using Opus 5.5?
author: rookan

replies.author: rookan
replies.body: Does AI work via Godot MCP or Godot directly? Any tips to setup efficient pipeline between Claude Code and Godot?

replies.author: RUSuper
replies.body: Claude is perfectly capable working in Godot without need for MCP, but you can use MCP, especially since without MCP you might get interrupted by constant opening of the project to take "before" and "after" screenshots. But I feel Godot is just engine that AI is more proficient at, graphic wise as long as it is stylistic you can push it real hard I feel like.

replies.author: warpedspoon
replies.body: I've been using Godot without the MCP. Can you elaborate? what happens instead of the before/after screenshots when you enable the mcp?

replies.author: RUSuper
replies.body: What it does give you is a live connection to the editor/running game, so the AI can read the scene tree, node properties and errors directly instead of guessing from pictures. depends a lot which one you use though, some barely do more than launch the project

replies.author: warpedspoon
replies.body: ah gotcha. any recommendations on which one?

replies.author: RUSuper
replies.body: I use Beckett one as it was free heh.

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body: Mcp. If you use it directly you could potentially corrupt your files. Mcp is the way to go.

comments.author: _Raro
comments.body: Godot as it is completely open source.

comments.author: Bluetails_Buizel
comments.body: Browser based is the fastest, it can write just the nessery engine that your game require so that it stays blazing fast on low end devices like mobile phones.

replies.author: FunkMunki
replies.body: I've been messing around with babylonjs lately and it's pretty smooth. They even have an editor.

comments.author: qing-turn
comments.body: I'm using Unity 6 with Claude Code and it works well. Claude edits the C# directly and runs builds and tests from the command line (Unity batchmode), so it can iterate without anyone clicking around in the editor. Godot is lighter and fully text-based, which AI also loves. For 3D I'd lean Unity for the tooling and assets, but either is fine as long as the AI can build and test from the command line.

replies.author: qing-turn
replies.body: CLI, no MCP. Claude runs Unity in batchmode (-batchmode -executeMethod ...) for builds, balance sims and regression tests, and edits the C# files directly. I almost never open the editor for it.

replies.author: caphohotain
replies.body: How to ask Claude to use CLI to do that?

comments.author: TehMasterer01
comments.body:
Custom graphics engine, custom game engine.

It’s the only way to make it not feel like yet another unity game.

comments.author: EdOfO
comments.body:
To an AI, the python of Godot, C# of Unity, and C++ of Unreal aren't that different to figure out. Unity & Unreal have a lot more documentation & help sites it can use for references, a lot more plugins, a lot more readymade assets, and a lot more features that make some game design things quicker.  
  
It still depends on the kind of game you want to make and how you want it to look and if you want to own it completely and sell it (then it's only Godot for you).
